findings.detail: EURUSD: BOS entry 695 trades, +0.077R, stop 0.1186%; IFVG entry 1,832 trades, +0.051R, stop 0.1066%; equilibrium entry 806 trades, +0.031R. QQQ: all negative (BOS -0.100R, IFVG -0.132R, EQ -0.195R). Allowing any inversion in the last 40 bars: 9,651 setups at -0.189R. Requiring the inversion on the previous bar: 3,465 setups at +0.051R.
findings.evidence: 'The stop shrinks on both, by 10 to 15%. Not the halving he describes'

findings.rule: TJR says the IFVG fires earlier than a BOS and gives a much better RR, and that he uses it almost more than BOS.
findings.detail: Quoted from his video transcripts: 'This makes my stop loss literally two times the size and now makes me have a risk-to-reward that's not even 1:0.5 ... versus if I take this trade up here, if I'm risking $1,000, I'll be able to make $1,300.' Also: 'I use this confluence almost every single day, almost more than break of structure, because more often than not it happens before break of structure.' A second spec cites 68 and 123 ticks of better entry.
findings.evidence: 'I use this confluence almost every single day, almost more than break of structure'

findings.rule: TJR himself says a fully automated, always-profitable bot of his strategy is not realistic, and he keeps room for discretion instead of giving a step-by-step.
findings.detail: Transcript quote reported by a third-party implementer. The author adds that the engine implements the sequence faithfully, but 'The part he says makes it work is the part that cannot be written down.'
findings.evidence: 'if we wanted to just make some sort of trading bot that automated our strategy ... and if that strategy actually gave us like 100% profitable results over a long period of time, then awesome. Everybody would be able to get rich.'

findings.rule: TJR rejects bar-replay backtesting because the higher-timeframe candle is shown already completed (lookahead). He counts only live and demo results. His 'backtest' is drilling about 10 examples per setup.
findings.detail: Bootcamp Day 42 per the spec. The implication for a bot: every HTF series must be truncated to its last completed candle at decision time. The implementer adds a warning: beating his numbers (WR much above 64% or RR much above 1:1.23) indicates a lookahead bug, and trading most days indicates a dropped stand-down filter.
findings.evidence: 'the higher timeframe candle is displayed already completed, so you are reading the future'; 'Beating his numbers is a bug report, not a success.'

findings.rule: Performance TJR states for his 2026 strategy: 64.29% win rate, average RR about 1:1.23 or 1:1.33 (sources disagree), about $22k average win vs $16k average loss, Jan-May 2026 no losing month.
findings.detail: From 'My UPDATED Day Trading Strategy (2026)' (video 8PYgFVB0GHE), via TradeZella journal. Broker account +$874,782 gross, 'over $700,000' net of fees. Jan ~$41k, Feb $148k, Mar $293k, Apr ~$230k, May ~$34k. May: +, -10k, -70k, +84k by week. CONFLICT: step436/step434 render the RR as 1:1.233 (transcript '123.3'); step72 and a Chinese research file render it 1:1.33. The $22k/$16k ratio (1.375) fits 1.33 better. He says his WR is understated because break-even exits minus fees are logged as losses. Older video (Strategy_Revealed, Apr-Oct): $1,047,984 in 6 months, average win $22k, average loss $11k, realized RR 'around 1 to 2 point something' after partials. These are unverified self-reports.
findings.evidence: 'my daily win rate is around 64% or 64.29%'; transcript renders RR as 'a 123.3', restated as '1 to 1.33'

findings.rule: TJR trades only a minority of sessions (about 7-15 trading days a month) and recommends one trade a day.
findings.detail: From the Data_Backed_Strategy_Everyday dashboard (e.g. April: 7 days, May: 10 days, June: 11 days) and bootcamp Day 29: 'I recommend one trade a day, that's what I do, one trade a day, sometimes I'll take two.' Day 21: take one trade, win or lose, and you're done. Alternative daily cap: risk 1-3% of the account per day (Day 13).
findings.evidence: 'take one trade and just go home... whether it's a win or a loss, you're done'

findings.rule: Swing definition TJR states: a high is an up candle followed by a down candle, at the higher of the two wicks. A low is a down candle followed by an up candle, at the lower wick.
findings.detail: Codable: high at bar i if close[i]>open[i] and close[i+1]<open[i+1], level = max(high[i], high[i+1]). Low mirrored with min(low). Two green candles in a row are not a high. Run separately per timeframe and never mix. The pivot can only be stamped on the second candle (causal). An implementer found this sits 35-44% closer to price than fractal swings on 12 instruments.
findings.evidence: 'a high consists of an up candle, then a down candle... we're looking for the highest wick of those two candlesticks'

findings.rule: A break of structure requires a candle BODY close strictly beyond the MOST RECENT opposite swing. A wick does not count, and a close equal to the level does not count.
findings.detail: In an uptrend watch only the most recent low; in a downtrend only the most recent high. Level = wick extreme, break = close. A higher low inside a downtrend changes nothing until the most recent high is closed above.
findings.evidence: 'We need a full candlestick body close above a high or underneath a low'; 'the candle body is equal with this low... We need the candle body to close underneath'

findings.rule: A sweep is only an 'opportunity'. A level that is traded through becomes a confirmed sweep only once a lower-timeframe BOS against it prints. If price just keeps going, it was never a sweep.
findings.detail: Never enter on the sweep alone. Mark all candidate levels, then wait for the reaction. Implement as: level breached -> PENDING; opposite body-close BOS on 5m (or 1m) -> CONFIRMED; continuation without BOS -> discard. Do not hunt sweeps on the 1-minute; levels come from 1H/4H.
findings.evidence: 'If price comes down and takes out a low and keeps going down, is it a liquidity sweep? No. Because it's not reacting to it... We wait for reaction.'

findings.rule: Levels TJR marks before the open: 1H and 4H highs/lows, Asia and London session highs/lows, New York session and pre-market highs/lows, previous day high/low, plus relative equal highs/lows and news-candle highs/lows.
findings.detail: Levels already pushed through with no reaction are dropped ('that draw on liquidity is pretty useless'). A replay that omitted the NY session and pre-market levels lost the most trades: adding them took it from 15 to 20 trades, and the 'no level pushed through' stand-downs fell from 90 to 9 symbol-days. On a London manipulation+reversal (continuation) day, he marks 5m/15m highs/lows and waits for one to be swept.
findings.evidence: 'Asia session highs, Asia session lows, London session highs, London session lows, New York highs, New York lows. All of these are significant draws on liquidity.'

findings.rule: TJR's session clock in New York time: Asia 18:00-03:00, London 03:00-08:30, New York 08:30-18:00 in one video but 09:30-17:00 in another, with 17:00-18:00 a 'spread hour'.
findings.detail: Quoted: '1800 to 3 is Asia session. 3 to 8:30 London session. 8:30 back to 1800 is New York session.' CONFLICT on NY: only_liquidity_guide gives 09:30-17:00, Advanced_Liquidity_Concepts gives 08:30-18:00. Another conflict: NY pre-market open is 08:30 (Time Theory) vs 08:00 (bias video). CONFLICT with third-party bots: gold-tactic uses Asia 00:00-07:00 UTC; the MES backtest uses Asia 20:00-02:00 ET; the smartmoneyconcepts library 'Asian kill zone' is 00:00-04:00 UTC.
findings.evidence: '1800 to 3 is Asia session. 3 to 8:30 London session. 8:30 back to 1800 is New York session.'

findings.rule: Intraday clock (ET): 09:30-09:50 manipulation window, 09:50-10:10 ideal entry ('macro'), no new trades after 10:30. No pre-market entries and no PM session.
findings.detail: Soft edges: 'I take trades at 10:20 sometimes. I take trades at 9:45 sometimes.' He declined a valid 11:05 setup because he did not want to sit through the chop. 2026 video: 'By 10:30, I'm done for the freaking day' if the indexes are not aligned. Pre-market: 'The answer is always going to be no', but a pre-market sweep that has already reacted counts as the day's sweep. Asia and London are for marking levels only. Bootcamp Day 29 variant: 'within that first hour and a half' of NYSE open.
findings.evidence: 'what I call our manipulation time frame, which is from 9:30 to 9:50'; 'from 9:50 to 10:10, we have our entry period'; 'if I can't find a trade by 10:30, I'm done for the day'

findings.rule: 2026 four-step sequence: (1) price pushes through a session/1H/4H level; (2) 5-min BOS or 5-min IFVG against the sweep; (3) 5-min pullback into equilibrium or an FVG; (4) on the 1-min, a counter BOS (the retrace) and then a BOS/IFVG back in the trade direction = entry.
findings.detail: His compression: 'We're looking for a liquidity sweep, 5 minute break of structure. Then we're looking for a one minute break of structure to the upside and then one minute break of structure to the downside. Awesome. We're entering right there.' Step 3 he folds into step 4 himself. Instruments: ES and NQ, and he takes the trade on whichever index produced the setup.
findings.evidence: 'a 5-minute break of structure or a 5-minute inverse fair value gap'; 'Scale down to the one minute time frame and look for a break of structure… or an inverse fair value gap'

findings.rule: ES/NQ alignment veto: no trade when the S&P 500 and NASDAQ 5-minute trends disagree. They can align later in the session.
findings.detail: Quoted: 'If the S&P 500 and the NASDAQ on the five minute are not aligned, I do not want to be taking a trade… the market is probably indecisive.' Also: 'if the indexes weren't aligned at the start of the session, that's fine. They can still get aligned later.' Coding pitfall: one bot's veto silently compared a symbol with itself on days the other index had stood down. Reality check: in round 72 the veto hurt ES/SPY results; in the replay, removing it raised trades from 16 to 25.
findings.evidence: 'if the S&P 500 and the NASDAQ on the five minute are not aligned, I do not want to be taking a trade.'

findings.rule: FVG definition TJR uses: three candles. Bullish if the low of candle 3 is above the high of candle 1 (bearish mirrored). It dies on a body CLOSE through it, never on a wick. On a stack of gaps, use the bottom gap for longs and the top gap for shorts.
findings.detail: An IFVG is a gap closed through against its bias. Equilibrium is the exact midpoint of the MOST RECENT swing low and swing high: buy below it, sell above it. He spent about 5 minutes warning against anchoring to an older swing. A gap is discarded if price continues without returning, and is never dragged forward in time.
findings.evidence: 'It dies on a candle CLOSING through it, never on a wick poking in.'

findings.rule: In his newest teaching TJR says he no longer uses order blocks or breaker blocks. The only continuation confluences are equilibrium and fair value gaps.
findings.detail: CONFLICT with older sources: bootcamp Days 20/22/24 rank order blocks as the first entry choice, and a third-party MT5 thesis EA still uses OB and Breaker. The implementer also lists SMT divergence and the 79% extension as dropped from the current strategy. But another implementer (aitrader) calls SMT 'his signature confluence, 20+ mentions', and a January 2026 course recap shows him using a bearish SMT to override his bias. So SMT status is disputed.
findings.evidence: 'I no longer use order blocks. I no longer use breaker blocks. The only continuation confluences that I need are equilibrium and fair value gaps.'

findings.rule: Stop goes beyond the swept extreme plus a spread buffer. The 2026 version places it 'above the second high' / 'below the second low' of the retrace. He never uses fixed-point, percentage or volatility stops.
findings.detail: Bootcamp Day 38: 'I almost always put my stop loss above the liquidity sweep.' Buffer: 'point five points below the actual price point, or figure out what your spread is'; he used about 4 points on one ES trade (the transcript is garbled). 'your stop loss... shouldn't be based purely off of points or pips.' Exception he dislikes: if the sweep is too far away, place it above a nearer FVG/OB. The 2026 'second high/low' is read by eye, so it is discretionary. Third-party variants: 2 ticks beyond the sweep candle (tjr-trading-assistant), 3 handles (sarahlees), 5 points (MT5 thesis).
findings.evidence: 'I almost always put my stop loss above the liquidity sweep.'; 2026: 'we can put our stop above the second high'

findings.rule: Profit taking: TP1 is the first draw on liquidity one timeframe above the execution timeframe, at least 1:1. Take about 50% there and move the stop to break-even, then use 3-4 targets at the next levels.
findings.detail: Day 54 recap: 'after take profit one got hit I took off 50 of the position.' Targets must not come from a lower timeframe than the BOS. Remainder stopped at break-even is normal. Realized RR after partials 'around 1 to 2 point something' (older video) vs 1:1.233 or 1:1.33 (2026). Third-party mechanical tests found flat 1.0R or smaller targets beat his stated RR.
findings.evidence: 'most of the time my first take profit is going to be minimum one to one'; 'take profit one gets hit, we can go ahead and move stop loss to break even, take partial profits'

findings.rule: Sizing: a fixed lot size calibrated so his NARROWEST typical stop risks 1% of the account, so wider stops risk 2-3%. Tiers are 0.5x (news day or bank-holiday eve), 1x, and 2x 'confident' (which he forbids for students).
findings.detail: Worked example: $100k account, 4-point stop, 1% risk, 25 lots. Quoted: 'That also means I'll be risking two percent of my account if we have a larger stop loss.' Confident tier: 'you guys should never use a confident lot size'. The set size is per instrument. Daily budget is 1-3% of the account. A losing streak means 2-3 losing WEEKS; his response is to demand more confluence (sweep + BOS + EQ or FVG), not to size down.
findings.evidence: 'what's usually the LOWEST your stop loss will be during a trade... That is going to be our SET lot size'

findings.rule: Never trade CPI, PPI, FOMC or NFP days. For other red-folder US news, wait until 15-20 minutes after the release and skip if it caused large wicks or moves. For a 10:00 release, wait until 10:30. Skip bank holidays and Fed chair speech days (and the day after).
findings.detail: Source: Forex Factory filtered to USD, yellow removed, grey kept for holidays. Quoted: 'CPI PPI FOMC and NFP those four… I do not trade whatsoever.' The 'large wicks, large moves' threshold is never quantified, so it is not codable as stated. De-risk to half size on news days. Replay impact: the news gate blocked 48 symbol-days but removing it added 0 trades, since other filters also failed. CONFLICT: sarahlees' NQ backtest reports its 8:30-9:10 window on CPI days at 75% WR, on a small, data-mined subset.
findings.evidence: 'if it's CPI PPI FOMC or NFP just call it quits bro sleep in live to trade another day'

findings.rule: Daily bias has two procedures that conflict. Taught (current): classify London's session profile. Performed live (bootcamp Days 47-55): the daily sets direction and the 4H or 1H must agree, else stand down. Trade only with the daily bias.
findings.detail: Profiles: (1) London consolidated -> NY manipulates and reverses; (2) London manipulated without reversing -> NY reverses; (3) London manipulated and reversed -> NY continues, but still needs a 5m/15m sweep. Live rule: 'at least I need the daily and the four hour to be in confluence'. The 1H stands in when the 4H is choppy (Days 49, 52, 54). Replay impact: the daily/4H veto caused 96 of 280 stand-downs; enforcing the trade side to the daily bias raised net from -$4,222 to -$190. 2026 course: the bias is a lean that an SMT divergence plus a BOS on both indexes can overrule; it held 88% of the time.
findings.evidence: 'can we go against daily bias no… we're going to stick to this bias until we're proved wrong.' (Day 49)

findings.rule: A bachelor's thesis coded the 'TJR framework' as an MT5 EA on NVIDIA (1-min, Jan 2025 to Mar 2026) and got a marginal edge: 275 trades, 43.64% WR, PF 1.18, +18.4%. The forward test lost.
findings.detail: Settings: 2% risk, trade window 08:30-16:00 ET, levels = PDH/PDL + last 3 H1 + last 2 H4 highs/lows (deduped within 50 points), sweep = bar beyond level + 5 points. Reversal: close beyond the extreme of the prior 5 M1 bars (BOS), or IFVG, or a close beyond 79% of the sweep leg. Continuation: touch of EQ/FVG/OB/Breaker plus a candle in the trade direction. SL = leg extreme ± 5 points. TP = nearest opposite level, else 3R. One setup/day, force close at session end. Results on $10k: +$1,838.54, max equity DD 9.37%, average win $101 vs average loss $67, max 8 consecutive losses. Forward test (demo, Apr 2026): 6 trades, PF 0.68, -$50. Pitfalls visible in the code: fixed ET offset of -5 with no DST handling, and a max holding time of 47h44m despite the 'force close at session end' rule.
findings.evidence: Backtest.html: 'Total Trades: 275... Profit Trades (% of total): 120 (43.64%)... Profit Factor: 1.18'

findings.rule: Asia-range sweep -> BOS -> FVG on MES/S&P 5-min: one repo claims a 77-79% WR at 2R, but the claim is suspect (in-sample, 13+ versions, longs only).
findings.detail: Data: 3-year S&P CFD (USA500IDXUSD) 2020-09 to 2023-09. Asia = 20:00-02:00 ET; killzones 02:00-05:00 and 08:30-11:30 ET. Setup: long only, 4H trend up (EMA50 slope), first wick below Asia low, BOS = close above the highest high of the last 30 minutes within 60 minutes, entry = limit at FVG midpoint within 60 minutes, stop = post-sweep low - 2 ticks, 2R target, 2-hour time exit. Reasons for skepticism: positive time exits count as wins, fills trigger on a touch, shorts underperform, 13+ versions were tried, no out-of-sample test, and the author sells indicators on Whop.
findings.evidence: 'Asia-low sweep → BOS → FVG entry on the 5-minute chart produced a 77–79% win rate at 2R over a 3-year sample'

findings.rule: NQ 1-min sweep -> MSS -> FVG (2022-2025, 409 trades) was best in the 08:30-09:10 ET pre-market/news window, better than 09:30-10:00 or 10:00-11:00.
findings.detail: Window A 08:30-09:10: 183 trades, 60.7% WR, PF 3.16. B 09:30-10:00: 77 trades, 49.4%, PF 2.47. C 10:00-11:00: 149 trades, 38.3%, PF 1.32. Overall 50.4% WR, +$259.72/trade, average win $948 vs average loss $439. Rules: SL 3 handles beyond the sweep candle, TP = nearest swing body, min 1:1, 20-bar sweep cooldown, stop after the first win, max 3 attempts/day, 0.5% risk. Caveat: QQQ 1-min scaled x40 as an NQ proxy (possibly the IEX feed, which elsewhere changed results by 0.2R). The news-combo win rates (71-75%) come from small, data-mined subsets. This conflicts with TJR's no-pre-market-entries rule.
findings.evidence: 'A | 60.7% | 3.16 | 183'; 'Uses QQQ ... as a free proxy for NQ futures, scaled x40'

findings.rule: The ICT Silver Bullet (sweep -> FVG in 1-hour windows) is net-negative in mechanical forward-accumulating tests on NQ/ES/CL, and the 'optimized' spec failed immediately in live forward data.
findings.detail: NQ 5-min, 1 contract, $10 costs: 30 trades, 33.3% WR, PF 0.68, -$3,895. ES: 39 trades, -0.13R average. Rules: windows 3-4am / 10-11am / 2-3pm NY, sweep = takes the prior 2-hour extreme and closes back inside, first FVG ≥0.5 point, limit at the near edge, stop 1 tick beyond the sweep, 2R, 2-hour time exit, same-bar stop+target counts as a loss. The Aug-18 optimized spec showed +0.49R/trade at selection, then -5.4R over its next 7 live trades. The 14-day re-optimizing walk-forward made 18 trades, +4.82R (fragile).
findings.evidence: 'the best-looking retro spec is mostly luck'

findings.rule: A YouTube Silver Bullet backtest on FX Replay claimed +44.4% in 45 days. A mechanical 5-year NQ 1-min replication of the same rules lost money.
findings.detail: Video: 15 trades, about 5:1 average RR. Mechanical (09:00 hourly range, sweep 10:00-11:00, displacement body ≥1.5×ATR(20) and ≥70% of range, FVG ≥0.3 ATR, min RR 2.5, BE at 3R), 2020-09 to 2025-11: 78 trades, 21.8% WR, -0.087R/trade, -6.75R total. By entry type: FVG 46 trades +0.044R, OB 15 trades +0.182R, Breaker 17 trades -0.678R.
findings.evidence: strategy.md: 'Total Return +44.4%' (video, 15 trades); computed from trades.csv: 78 trades, 21.8% win, mean -0.087R

findings.rule: 'Target the opposite-side liquidity' often makes the planned reward smaller than the stop. On XAUUSD, a 57% WR still produced -0.28R.
findings.detail: 17,399 trades, 108 settings, 2020-2026 Dukascopy gold. Median planned RR 0.44:1. Only 3/108 settings were positive in all 3 chronological splits, and 0 of those had 15+ out-of-sample trades. With real Silver Bullet killzones enforced (NY hours 3, 10, 14): 5,010 trades, -0.55R; fixed 1:2 target -0.35R; 0/162 settings positive in all splits. Entry at the next bar's open after the FVG touch; swings only once confirmed.
findings.evidence: 'the median setup risks more than twice what it targets'

findings.rule: A falsification-style study of multi-timeframe SMC found no replicable edge: 0/210 config×instrument cells, walk-forward -0.329R.
findings.detail: 42 pre-registered configs × 5 instruments (XAUUSD, EURUSD, GBPUSD, GBPJPY, WTI), 2015-2022, M1 intrabar fills, BH-FDR. Best pooled expectancy +0.004R (p=0.49). Walk-forward 95% CI [-0.416, -0.228]; 11/12 periods negative. Performance was inside the random-entry null band. Three lookahead bugs were found late: take-profit swings used before confirmation, a filled limit order cancelled by its own bar's close, and a stop inside the fill bar ignored.
findings.evidence: '0 / 210 (config × instrument) cells survive the cross-instrument BH-FDR'

findings.rule: A long-only NQ bot (5-min IFVG retest inside an active 15-min bull FVG, 09:30-12:00 ET, 2R) reports a positive 3-year backtest. It is long-only in a rising market, and shorts were much weaker.
findings.detail: Jan 2023 to May 2026, Databento 5-min, 1 MNQ: 432 trades, 53.5% WR, PF about 2.3, +$17,187, max DD $786, every year positive (2023 WR 46.5% up to 2026 68.1%). Stop = 5m FVG bottom - 2 points, entry at the next bar's open, exit by 15:45 ET. Shorts: 42.5% WR vs 56.5% for longs. Its predecessor was retired for 'marginal real-world edge'. This is not TJR's exact model, but it is the IFVG-heavy style he describes.
findings.evidence: 'Trades: 432 over 3 years... Win Rate: 53.5%... Profit Factor: ~2.3'

findings.rule: The popular Python 'smartmoneyconcepts' library (about 2k stars) uses future bars. swing_highs_lows uses a centered window (shift(-swing_length//2)) and fvg uses shift(-1). A user reported this inflated a backtest from PF 1.82 to 7.32.
findings.detail: XAUUSD M15, 10 years: centered window 177 trades, 81.4% WR, PF 7.32. Causal confirm-bars version: 106 trades, 52.8% WR, PF 1.82. Also, bos_choch writes the BOS at an earlier swing index, with BrokenIndex recorded later. Session defaults are fixed UTC with no DST. Fix: confirm a pivot only after N later bars, lag every signal to its confirmation bar, and use 'America/New_York' time zones.
findings.evidence: 'Centered window (current) | 177 | 81.4% | 7.32; No look-ahead (confirm bars) | 106 | 52.8% | 1.82'

findings.rule: Reading the still-forming higher-timeframe candle (e.g. the current 1H or 4H bar) for bias is a lookahead bug. Every HTF value must come from the last COMPLETED candle.
findings.detail: One implementer found its HTF bias read the hourly candle in progress, whose high and low include 5-min bars that had not happened yet: 'that is the exact mechanism behind the Nasdaq result.' The cryptobot TJR bot passes five truncation tests: a 4H candle starting 08:00 does not exist at 10:00, pivots are stamped on the second candle, and all 16 real entries were re-decided with future bars deleted and came out identical. The multi-timeframe rule: the 5-min confirmation bar must have closed before any 1-min bar is consulted.
findings.evidence: 'every one of the 16 real entries was re-decided with every later bar deleted from memory, and all 16 came back identical'

findings.rule: Optimistic fill assumptions turn a zero-edge ICT strategy into an apparent positive one. Requiring price to trade through the limit and letting stops gap costs about 0.06R per trade.
findings.detail: QQQ, 447 trades: touch fills with stops filled exactly at the stop: -0.001R. Price must trade through the level: -0.013R. Plus stops that gap-fill at the open: -0.060R. Other bugs: a 'trade-through' tick of 0.01 wiped out all EURUSD fills and silently reported NO TRADES; no minimum stop distance produced R multiples in the millions (divide by near-zero); a drawdown gate locked out permanently (733 silent refusals); costs charged as % of notional understated futures costs about 5x vs per-contract costs.
findings.evidence: 'Realistic execution costs 0.059R per trade, and most of that is gapped stops.'

findings.rule: Because TJR-style stops are tiny (especially on 1-min triggers), fixed costs eat a large share of R. Measure costs in R, not in % of notional.
findings.detail: At a 0.05% stop: EURUSD 0.032R, QQQ 0.200R, BTC 1.200R per trade. Futures NQ/ES: about 0.04-0.06R cost drag. SPY/QQQ 1-min trigger: a 0.04% round trip = 0.48R at a 0.084% median stop. TJR himself notes fees are material: $874,782 gross vs about $700k net in TradeZella. The replay paper broker uses maker entry (resting limit) and taker exit plus slippage.
findings.evidence: 'EURUSD | 0.032R; QQQ | 0.200R; BTC | 1.200R'

findings.rule: The data feed alone can swing the results of a wick-based sweep strategy by about 0.2R. Free IEX-only equity feeds under-report wicks, and yfinance caps 1m/5m history at about 60 days.
findings.detail: Same QQQ, same 60 days: Yahoo consolidated tape 35 trades, +0.005R, 71.4% WR vs Alpaca free IEX 44 trades, -0.206R, 56.8% WR. Wick/range: QQQ IEX 0.457, QQQ Yahoo 0.526, NQ futures 0.538, NSXUSD 0.536, Dukascopy Nasdaq CFD 0.571. Recommendation: use real exchange futures data (e.g. Databento, IBKR about $10-15/month) and cross-check against a second vendor. The IBKR API serves at most 3,500 5-min bars per pull (about 13.5 days).
findings.evidence: '0.211R and fifteen points of win rate, from the data source alone.'

findings.rule: Multiple-testing and selection bias dominate ICT/TJR backtests. Charge every tested variant, hold out a sealed test set, and require a positive walk-forward plus second-market replication.
findings.detail: Examples: 335 combinations produced +0.174R in-sample and -0.131R out of sample. With 12 strategies and about 350 trades, a result must clear +0.126R (1 SE = 0.064R), and the expected best-by-luck is +0.091R. Across 516 configurations, luck produces +0.068R. The Silver Bullet v2 spec (+0.49R) lost -5.4R live. Nasdaq CFD +0.223R passed 13/13 parameter nudges and 9/10 time blocks, yet the second source was needed to judge it. Robustness checks confirm consistency, not tradeability.
findings.evidence: 'A result is not real until it has cleared its own confidence interval, survived being charged for every hypothesis tested to find it, held up on data it was not chosen on, and reproduced on a feed from a different vendor.'
